questions.answer:
Step 1: Perform the matrix multiplication.
First, multiply the \(1 \times 2\) row vector by the \(2 \times 2\) matrix:
\[
\begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & \sin\theta \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta & 2\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta \end{bmatrix}
\]
Next, multiply this result by the \(2 \times 1\) column vector:
\[
k = (6\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta)\cos\theta + (2\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta)\sin\theta
\]
\[
k = 6\cos^2\theta + 4\sin\theta\cos\theta + 3\sin^2\theta
\]

Step 2: Express the quadratic trigonometric terms using double-angle identities.
Recall the standard identities:
\[
\cos^2\theta = \frac{1 + \cos(2\theta)}{2}, \quad \sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}, \quad 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \sin(2\theta)
\]
Substitute these into the expression for \(k\):
\[
k = 6\left(\frac{1 + \cos(2\theta)}{2}\right) + 3\left(\frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\right) + 2\sin(2\theta)
\]
\[
k = 3(1 + \cos(2\theta)) + \frac{3}{2}(1 - \cos(2\theta)) + 2\sin(2\theta)
\]
\[
k = \frac{9}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos(2\theta) + 2\sin(2\theta)
\]

Step 3: Maximize the resulting trigonometric expression.
For real constants \(A\) and \(B\), the maximum value of \(A\cos\phi + B\sin\phi\) is \(\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}\). Here, \(A = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(B = 2\):
\[
\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{4} + \frac{16}{4}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{4}} = \frac{5}{2}
\]
Thus, the maximum value of \(k\) is:
\[
k_{\text{max}} = \frac{9}{2} + \frac{5}{2} = 7
\]

Misconception Analysis:
- Choice A (6) results from ignoring the cross-product term \(4\sin\theta\cos\theta\) and merely selecting the maximum diagonal entry.
- Choice C (9) results from taking the trace (sum of diagonal entries) of the matrix.
- Choice D (14) results from calculating the determinant of the matrix, \(6(3) - 2(2) = 14\).

questions.q: If matrix \( A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \) and matrix \( B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \), what is the matrix \( 2A + B \)?
questions.answer:
To find the matrix \( 2A + B \), first perform scalar multiplication by multiplying each entry of matrix \( A \) by \( 2 \):
\[ 2A = 2\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2(3) & 2(-2) \\ 2(0) & 2(4) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 8 \end{bmatrix} \]

Next, add the corresponding entries of \( 2A \) and \( B \):
\[ 2A + B = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 8 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 + (-1) & -4 + 5 \\ 0 + 2 & 8 + (-3) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \]

Common Errors:
- \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) is obtained by simply computing \( A + B \) without multiplying by the scalar \( 2 \).
- \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) results from mistakenly multiplying only the first entry of \( A \) by \( 2 \).
- \(\begin{bmatrix} 7 & -9 \\ -2 & 11 \end{bmatrix}\) results from computing \( 2A - B \) instead of \( 2A + B \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix} \) and \( B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\0&4\end{bmatrix} \), find \( AB \).
questions.answer: \( (AB)_{11}=-2\cdot1+0\cdot0=-2 \), and similarly for the other three entries: \( AB=\begin{bmatrix}-2&2\\0&-4\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\0&-2\end{bmatrix} \) and \( B=\begin{bmatrix}3&4\\2&4\end{bmatrix} \), find \( AB \).
questions.answer: \( (AB)_{11}=1\cdot3+-2\cdot2=-1 \), and similarly for the other three entries: \( AB=\begin{bmatrix}-1&-4\\-4&-8\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&-3\\-3&-2\end{bmatrix} \) and \( B=\begin{bmatrix}4&-4\\1&4\end{bmatrix} \), find \( AB \).
questions.answer: \( (AB)_{11}=-4\cdot4+-3\cdot1=-19 \), and similarly for the other three entries: \( AB=\begin{bmatrix}-19&4\\-14&4\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&1\\-3&-5\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\-1\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -3(-2)+1(-1)=5 \), second entry \( -3(-2)+-5(-1)=11 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\11\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-5&0\\-2&5\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-3\\4\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -5(-3)+0(4)=15 \), second entry \( -2(-3)+5(4)=26 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}15\\26\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&0\\3&1\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\5\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -4(3)+0(5)=-12 \), second entry \( 3(3)+1(5)=14 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-12\\14\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-2\\-3&-3\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -3(0)+-2(-6)=12 \), second entry \( -3(0)+-3(-6)=18 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}12\\18\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: Suppose that \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&0\\1&5\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -3(5)+0(6)=-15 \), second entry \( 1(5)+5(6)=35 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-15\\35\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: Suppose that \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&-1\\-3&-4\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -2(0)+-1(-6)=6 \), second entry \( -3(0)+-4(-6)=24 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\24\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\-2\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( 2(-1)+-2(-2)=2 \), second entry \( -2(-1)+2(-2)=-2 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-2\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&-2\\-5&5\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-3\\0\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -2(-3)+-2(0)=6 \), second entry \( -5(-3)+5(0)=15 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\15\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\-4&-1\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\4\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( 0(-1)+-1(4)=-4 \), second entry \( -4(-1)+-1(4)=0 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-4\\0\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\5&3\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\-6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( 3(-1)+1(-6)=-9 \), second entry \( 5(-1)+3(-6)=-23 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-9\\-23\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&-1\\-3&4\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\-6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -4(-2)+-1(-6)=14 \), second entry \( -3(-2)+4(-6)=-18 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}14\\-18\end{bmatrix} \).

questions.q: Assuming that \( A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&4\\1&0\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\6\end{bmatrix} \), find \( A\mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer: Row-by-vector: first entry \( -4(5)+4(6)=4 \), second entry \( 1(5)+0(6)=5 \), so \( A\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\5\end{bmatrix} \).
